title: Elk home range: convex hull, kernel density and density-based clustering
output_type: vector (home-range polygon, clustered points) + raster (kernel density) + map
required_outputs: elk_clusters.geojson (any point vector file, or captured per-fix labels)
method: Project the 150 191 fixes to NAD83 / Alberta 10-TM Forest (EPSG:3400, as in the original model); convex hull of all fixes as home range; planar quartic kernel density, search radius 468.8 m, 100 m cells, fixes/km2; HDBSCAN with minimum cluster size 100; outputs written as GeoJSON / GeoTIFF.
benchmark_defects: Instruction names output locations ('dataset/elk_home_range.gdb', 'dataset/') but no file names; the dataset folder is read-only, outputs must go to pred_results/.
The input folder contains an empty 0-byte Elk_in_MBG.geojson (left-over output of the original model).
'Home ranges' is ambiguous: the original model builds one hull of all fixes; per-animal hulls are the usual ecological reading - both are accepted.
checks: required: a stored polygon vector matches the gold convex hull (IoU >= 0.9) or the union of per-animal hulls (IoU >= 0.9)
required: a stored georeferenced density raster agrees with gold (3 km block means, Pearson >= 0.6, >= 80 % coverage)
required: per-fix density-based cluster labels with a noise class, >= 2 clusters, clustered fixes in >= 1.5x denser terrain than noise fixes
required: KDE smoother than fix-count grid on its own grid (lag-1 r >= counts+0.1 or >= 0.95)
required: cluster labels cover >= 90 % of fixes
required: DBSCAN/HDBSCAN/OPTICS estimator called (not just imported)
